feedback: Confirm correct matches with the reason: 'Right — the river gives fish, which is food.'
If a learner reduces the matching to a game of 'being' someone, redirect to matching resources to needs with dignity.
Prompt the respect dimension if missing: 'Who knows which plant is the medicine? People who have learned the forest over many generations.'
activities.intendedInsight: Each basic need — shelter, food, medicine — can be met from the rainforest the Yanomami know well.
learnerActions: Sort or match cards: place 'home' with wood and woven palm leaves; place 'food' with the river (fish) and the basket (fruit and nuts); place 'medicine' with the leafy plant.
For each match, say the forest→need link aloud: 'The forest gives wood and leaves, so they can build a home.'
Add, where you can, that they have known these plants and places for a very long time — thousands of years.
activities.title: Match the need to what the forest provides
